title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the cycle life of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 5 micrometers. The anode support contains nickel oxide and scandia-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The solid electrolyte of scandia-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The cell can be operated at 600 to 750 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved high-voltage stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.045 or less. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Composite cathode comprising lithium sulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises lithium sulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The lithium sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. The p-toluenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 105 degrees C storage. The solid electrolyte is the conductive polymer layer that serves as the true cathode of the capacitor. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the tantalum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The equivalent series resistance is 5 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 5 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The tantalum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of tantalum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polyaniline doped with p-toluenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 5 milliohms or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a lanthanum strontium manganite electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the nitrogen oxide concentration. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 400 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium manganite electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising lanthanum fluoride, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 8 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 650 to 800 degrees C is described. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the scandia-stabilized zirconia cell. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 8 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which lithium sulfide is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyethylene oxide and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. The solid electrolyte layer of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers and a relative density of 97%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 650 to 800 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The thin 10 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. The anode support contains nickel oxide and lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C
abstract: Described is a solid electrolytic capacitor element whose leakage current is reduced by a repair step of the dielectric film. The capacitor rated at 25 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The equivalent series resistance is 5 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The niobium capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous niobium anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polypyrrole particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising gadolinium-doped ceria; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% with the electrolyte. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the titanium disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The carbon coating on the titanium disulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing titanium disulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the titanium disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The yttria-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The LLZO, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles. The aluminum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The equivalent series resistance is 8 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 8 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The anode body is a sintered pellet of aluminum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous aluminum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Mixed potential type ammonia sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of barium carbonate that converts the ammonia concentration into an ionic activity. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The multilayer structure with the lanthanum fluoride ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The protective layer improves the durability of the lanthanum fluoride sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The ceramic is lanthanum fluoride and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The capacity retention of 85% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee_raw: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY IDNUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
assignee_db_group: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY IDNUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%.

title: Composite cathode comprising lithium sulfide and porous carbon and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which lithium sulfide is confined in the pores of porous carbon to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The carbon coating on the lithium sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 5 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 650 to 800 degrees C is described. The anode support contains nickel oxide and gadolinium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with niobium and sintered with Al2O3 is described. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 700 to 850 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 96%. The yttria-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2.
