The LATP, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Disclosed is a thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The reversible cell with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The solid electrolyte layer of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a relative density of 98%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 600 to 750 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Composite cathode comprising iron sulfide and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. A lithium-sulfur battery with the iron sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The active material iron sulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria with a thickness of 3 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The cell operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor having a porous niobium anode body and a hybrid electrolyte
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. The naphthalenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 125 degrees C storage. The equivalent series resistance is 10 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous niobium anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and vinylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 1 wt%. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 600 to 750 degrees C. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The anode support contains nickel oxide and scandia-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The solid electrolyte of scandia-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 300 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to sulfur dioxide against interfering gases. The sensor operating at 300 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for sulfur dioxide. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 300 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium nitrite and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The limiting current is proportional to the sulfur dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The solid electrolyte of sodium beta-alumina conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of sulfur dioxide.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The LATP and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of sodium carbonate that converts the ammonia concentration into an ionic activity. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for ammonia. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The lanthanum strontium manganite electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 10 seconds to a step change of ammonia concentration at 700 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 5 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 5 micrometers. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The solid electrolyte of samarium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The samarium-doped ceria electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.
