The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Composite cathode comprising titanium disulfide and porous carbon and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises titanium disulfide impregnated in porous carbon and a carbon coating on the composite. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 2 mg/cm2. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

assignee_raw: UNIVERSITY OF BELUNEA INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COPERATION FOUNDATION
assignee_db_group: UNIVERSITY OF BELUNEA INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which carbon dioxide is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 300 degrees C. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the carbon dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting carbon dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising sodium beta-alumina; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 300 degrees C.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. A solid electrolyte of polyaniline replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The p-toluenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 105 degrees C storage. The capacitor has a capacitance of 220 microfarads, a rated voltage of 16 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 5 milliohms at 100 kHz. The aluminum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polyaniline layer to serve as the cathode lead-out.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of aluminum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polyaniline doped with p-toluenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 5 milliohms or less.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The uniaxial pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polycarbonate based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polycarbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 92% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which hydrogen is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The ceramic is NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: niobium solid electrolytic capacitor having a low equivalent series resistance
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous niobium anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising polyaniline doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the niobium anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The equivalent series resistance is 8 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous niobium anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with silica nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with silica nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate solid electrolyte for detecting sulfur dioxide
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The protective layer improves the durability of the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate sensor in an exhaust gas. The multilayer structure with the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The limiting current is proportional to the sulfur dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting sulfur dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 0.5 wt%. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Mixed potential type oxygen sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting oxygen comprises a NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising platinum, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for oxygen.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. The solid electrolyte of samarium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 5 micrometers. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 97% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Multilayer ceramic gas sensor element and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. A lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode may be used for detecting carbon dioxide at 700 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for oxygen. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of oxygen concentration at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising lanthanum fluoride, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the sodium beta-alumina sensor in an exhaust gas. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for ammonia. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising sodium beta-alumina, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The roll pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Lithium fluoride-rich halide interlayer protecting a lithium metal negative electrode from a sulfide solid electrolyte
abstract: A protective interlayer disposed between a lithium metal negative electrode and a sulfide solid electrolyte layer comprises a lithium fluoride-rich halide composition represented by Li(3-w)Y(1-w)Cl(6-6w)F(6w), wherein 0.1 <= w <= 0.3, in which fluoride partially replaces chloride so that the halide is thermodynamically stable against metallic lithium while retaining an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The interlayer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers and is formed by casting a slurry of the halide powder and a fluorinated binder onto the lithium foil, or by applying a halide coating of the composition to the surface of the sulfide solid electrolyte layer facing the negative electrode. A thin LiF-rich passivation film of 5 nm to 30 nm forms spontaneously at the lithium side upon first contact and blocks electron leakage, so that the reductive decomposition of the sulfide solid electrolyte is suppressed and the electrochemical window of the cell is extended on the reduction side to 0 V. A lithium metal cell comprising the interlayer shows an interfacial resistance of 15 ohm cm2 or less and operates for 400 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 without short circuit.
first_claim: 1. An interlayer for a lithium metal cell, disposed between a lithium metal negative electrode and a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, the interlayer comprising a halide composition represented by Li(3-w)Y(1-w)Cl(6-6w)F(6w), wherein 0.1 <= w <= 0.3, wherein the interlayer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 15 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. A power density of 1.2 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. The scandia-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 15 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

assignee_raw: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
assignee_db_group: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

assignee_raw: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
assignee_db_group: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS HNRIEM
