The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyacrylic acid binder
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises titanium disulfide impregnated in porous carbon and a carbon coating on the composite. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the titanium disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. A 3 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The uniaxial pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Composite cathode comprising lithium sulfide and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The warm isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which nickel sulfide is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. Polysulfide dissolution from the nickel sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the nickel sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

assignee_db_group: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a titanium disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyvinylidene fluoride. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of titanium disulfide. The carbon coating on the titanium disulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Method for forming a conductive polymer layer on a dielectric oxide of a solid electrolytic capacitor
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The anode body is a sintered pellet of niobium powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. The equivalent series resistance is 10 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous niobium anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polypyrrole particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises lithium sulfide impregnated in porous carbon and a carbon coating on the composite. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with porous carbon by ball milling. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polycarbonate matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises iron sulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The active material iron sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The iron sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

assignee_raw: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
assignee_db_group: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Co., Ltd.
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved cycle life and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 5 micrometers. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 500 to 650 degrees C. The yttria-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the tantalum anode. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. A capacitance of 100 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The tantalum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The tantalum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a tantalum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 16 V.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for sulfur dioxide with improved response time
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which sulfur dioxide is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor detects sulfur dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The protective layer improves the durability of the sodium beta-alumina sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of sulfur dioxide.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 5 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 700 to 850 degrees C is described. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 5 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

assignee_raw: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
assignee_db_group: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a magnesium additive. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, carbon nanotubes, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded.
