A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polycarbonate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium difluorophosphate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The 1.0 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 700 to 850 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The anode support contains nickel oxide and lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 97% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. With 1 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. With 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The capacity retention of 88% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Potentiometric carbon dioxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 400 degrees C. A lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode may be used for detecting carbon dioxide at 400 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 10 seconds to a step change of carbon dioxide concentration at 400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to carbon dioxide against interfering gases. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium nitrite and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The solid electrolyte of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium nitrite in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects carbon dioxide.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for sulfur dioxide with improved response time
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 300 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The auxiliary electrode of sodium carbonate makes the sensor selective to sulfur dioxide against interfering gases. The limiting current is proportional to the sulfur dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of sulfur dioxide.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the scandia-stabilized zirconia cell. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 8 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. A solid electrolyte of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the tantalum anode. The anode body is a sintered pellet of tantalum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of tantalum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with naphthalenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 15 milliohms or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the scandia-stabilized zirconia cell. The reversible cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The anode support contains nickel oxide and scandia-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 10 micrometers. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite is a dense ceramic of 97% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 10 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing alumina nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 500 to 650 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 8 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 500 to 650 degrees C is described. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. The thin 8 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 0.8 W/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 97% or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. The thin 3 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The cell operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. The lanthanum strontium manganite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 700 to 850 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 700 to 850 degrees C. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 10 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The solid electrolyte layer of scandia-stabilized zirconia conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The lanthanum strontium manganite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 650 to 800 degrees C. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 10 micrometers. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a nickel sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. With 0.5 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The capacity retention of 92% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V.
