The capacity retention of 85% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone is also described.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the niobium anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polyaniline layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor has a capacitance of 330 microfarads, a rated voltage of 6.3 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 15 milliohms at 100 kHz. A solid electrolyte of polyaniline replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The capacitor rated at 6.3 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of niobium; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polyaniline doped with polystyrene sulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 15 milliohms or less.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The warm isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less.

assignee_db_group: DALANE UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. A 10 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Potentiometric carbon dioxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The multilayer structure with the yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The limiting current is proportional to the carbon dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. A power density of 1.2 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.2 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 600 to 750 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. The anode support contains nickel oxide and lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Composite cathode comprising iron sulfide and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a iron sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the iron sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing iron sulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the iron sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li3PS4 material. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C
abstract: Described is a solid electrolytic capacitor element whose leakage current is reduced by a repair step of the dielectric film. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 47 microfarad rating. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the tantalum capacitor. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles. The tantalum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 125 degrees C storage. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 15 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of tantalum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polyaniline doped with polystyrene sulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 15 milliohms or less.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium difluorophosphate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. With 1 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LiPON layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The lanthanum strontium manganite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polycarbonate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Mixed potential type hydrogen sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of hydrogen concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The lanthanum strontium manganite electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting hydrogen, comprising: a ceramic body comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 300 degrees C.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%.

assignee_raw: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.
