The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The active material sulfur is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 10 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. A power density of 1.2 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The cell can be operated at 700 to 850 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The solid electrolyte of yttria-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 98% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In the trigonal structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 30 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria with a thickness of 8 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 700 to 850 degrees C. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The stack of 50 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The cell operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising samarium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 8 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. With 2 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for ammonia with improved response time
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 500 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The ammonia sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The capacity retention of 88% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and LiF material. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. A power density of 1.0 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive in an amount of 0.5 wt%. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. With 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which nickel sulfide is confined in the pores of carbon nanotubes to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. Polysulfide dissolution from the nickel sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, carbon nanotubes, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Potentiometric nitrogen oxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium nitrite and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to nitrogen oxide against interfering gases. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium nitrite in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the cycle life of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: This disclosure concerns a surface mount capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode and a lead frame. The capacitor has a capacitance of 470 microfarads, a rated voltage of 10 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 15 milliohms at 100 kHz. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The anode body is a sintered pellet of aluminum powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The p-toluenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 105 degrees C storage.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of aluminum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polyaniline doped with p-toluenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 15 milliohms or less.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which silver is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The anode support contains nickel oxide and gadolinium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The solid electrolyte layer of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 5 micrometers and a relative density of 98%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 700 to 850 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 700 to 850 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The capacitor has a capacitance of 220 microfarads, a rated voltage of 16 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 20 milliohms at 100 kHz. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the aluminum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. A solid electrolyte of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The capacitor rated at 16 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the aluminum anode.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. A lithium-sulfur battery with the titanium disulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The titanium disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, carbon nanotubes, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polycarbonate matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polycarbonate based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Mixed potential type oxygen sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of sodium nitrite that converts the oxygen concentration into an ionic activity. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to oxygen against interfering gases. The ceramic is lanthanum fluoride and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The sensor detects oxygen with high selectivity and a response time of 2 seconds. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of oxygen.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2 mA/cm2. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 97%. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 600 to 750 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 600 to 750 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 600 to 750 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of scandia-stabilized zirconia conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa.
